title: L.N. Mattei Cap Corse Blanc
about: Louis-Napoléon Mattei was born in 1849 in Ersa, at the northern tip of Cap Corse, the narrow peninsula that runs north from Bastia. As a young man he kept a shop in Bastia selling coffee, tobacco, wine and liqueurs, and in the early 1870s he began distilling Corsican cédrat, the thick-skinned citron of the cape, into his own liqueurs. The house counts 1872 as its founding year, and its shop on Bastia’s Place Saint-Nicolas is now a listed historic monument. Its importer notes that the house still carries out its own macerations, ageing and bottling.

The Blanc is a quinquina blanc, a white aperitif wine bittered with cinchona bark, and an unusual style even among French aperitif wines. Its base is entirely mistelle: Vermentinu and Muscat Petits Grains must from the north of Corsica, its fermentation stopped with neutral alcohol to keep the natural grape sugar, with no sweetener added. Macerations of cinchona bark and of the cape’s cédrat give it bitterness, a citrus perfume and a silky texture. It is bottled at 17% alcohol.

In the glass it is a pale golden amber. Honeysuckle, elderflower and mixed herbs lead on the nose, followed by a quinine bitterness that builds across the palate, and the finish brings lemon zest, white pepper and the minerality and acidity of the Vermentinu. It is served chilled and neat over ice, or with a splash of tonic and a twist of orange zest.
